questions.question: Which of the following is a west-flowing peninsular river that forms an estuary instead of a delta?
questions.explanation: Narmada flows west through a rift valley and forms an estuary. The other three rivers listed here, Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery, form deltas on the east coast. This is a comparison of these options, not a rule for every east-flowing river. Source: NCERT, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, pp. 23-24.

questions.question: The Brahmaputra river is known by which name in Tibet?
questions.explanation: Brahmaputra is called Tsangpo in Tibet, Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, and Brahmaputra in Assam.

questions.question: Which doab lies between the Beas and Sutlej rivers?
questions.explanation: Bist Doab lies between Beas and Sutlej. Bari = Beas-Ravi. Rechna = Ravi-Chenab. Chaj = Chenab-Jhelum.

questions.question: How many states fall in the catchment area of the Godavari river?
questions.explanation: The catchment includes parts of seven states: Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Odisha. Count the drainage basin, including tributary catchments, rather than only states crossed by the main river. Source: CWC, Monitoring (South), Basin Details (Godavari row).

questions.question: The Luni river, originating from the Pushkar Valley, ends in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Luni drains towards the Rann of Kutch. It is an example of inland drainage, not the only inland-drainage river in India. Source: NCERT, India: Physical Environment, Chapter 3, p. 24.
